after.eli5: Washouts usually come after the market has already fallen. SPY was usually higher 3–6 months later, but days with the same drop did just as well, so the bounce comes from buying lower, not from breadth itself. Often it dipped further first.
after.src: Table: this page’s 50-day line and SPY closes (price only), about 1, 3 and 6 months later; a horizon still in the future shows –. Study tiles: the 2013+ study: 23 washouts, 3-month median +6.2% (17 of 22 up) vs +4.3% any day; days with a similar fall did +6.4%. 2021+ alone: +9.0%, up 6 of 9.

thrust.sub: A thrust is when the share of Russell 2000 stocks above their 50-day jumps from washed-out to strong within a few weeks
thrust.asof: as of the Nov 6 close · Russell 2000 breadth and IWM update after each close
thrust.l1: Needs a close at the fire line on or before Nov 9 (1 session left).
thrust.now: Armed: the line closed at 40.9% on Nov 6. A close at the fire line by Nov 9 would be a thrust; if not, the window lapses.
thrust.ct: Russell 2000 % above 50-day, last 4 months · yellow band = the window
thrust.ct2: IWM over the 3 months after each past thrust
thrust.how: ARMED: the line dropped to the arm line, which starts a clock of a few weeks. FIRED: it reached the fire line before the clock ran out, which is a thrust. IDLE: no clock is running.
thrust.src: History: Russell 2000 breadth history to Oct 1, 2026 for the 15 thrusts in the lower chart, our own count of today’s members after it. The line above is our own count. IWM closes split-adjusted.

storms.sub: SPY against its 200-day average · below it, the same VIX has come with bigger moves
storms.l1: A fall of about 0.7% would put it below.
storms.l2: SPY 735.29 · 200-day 730.38. Says how rough, not which way.
storms.cap: grey = what VIX expected · colour = how much SPY really moved the next month (2013+ averages, % a year). VIX usually guesses high.
storms.ct: SPY, last 2 years · red = days SPY closed below its 200-day average
storms.how: VIX is the options market’s guess of how much stocks will move, and it usually guesses high. Above the 200-day, next month’s real moves came in well under it (12.5 against 16.1). Below it they came in only a little under (24.1 against 27.1): at the same VIX, moves below the line ran about 20% bigger.
storms.now: SPY is 0.7% above its 200-day average: the calm side, where next month’s real moves have come in well under what VIX expected (12.5 against 16.1). It has been above since Apr 8, 2026.
storms.src: Study: SPY against its 200-day average, 2013+ (2,930 days above, 508 below). How much SPY really moved means its realised volatility over the next month, as a yearly rate, against VIX that day.

now.line: The 50-day line has been above the 200-day line since Oct 21 (13 sessions).
now.more: Before that, the 50-day line was below the 200-day line for 71 sessions (from Jul 13). It is the first golden cross since the washout of Sep 28. At the Nov 6 close the 50-day line is 5.4 points above the 200-day line, a gap of 27 stocks. It is a big cross: the first in a month or more. 16 of 27 big golden crosses since 2013 flipped back within a week. This one held through its first week.

text.eli5: When more S&P 500 stocks are above their 50-day average than above their 200-day, the blue line is on top: a golden cross. When fewer are, orange is on top: a death cross.
text.how: Blue is the share of S&P 500 stocks above their 50-day average, orange the share above their 200-day. They cross often and most crosses flip back within days, so the tables list the big ones: the first cross after a month or more the other way. A star marks a golden cross that is the first after a washout, or a death cross during a washout. Each row shows SPY about 1, 3 and 6 months later and its worst dip in the 3 months after the cross. The summary’s washout rows count every first golden cross after a washout, big or not.
text.src: Data: this page’s 50-day and 200-day lines for the S&P 500 and SPY closes (price only), since 2013. Big = the first cross after a month or more the other way. Uptrend = SPY above its 200-day average with that average higher than a month before. A horizon still in the future shows –.
